Figure: Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research.
pages.summary:
This page provides an overview of the anatomy of the esophagus, describing it as a flattened muscular tube measuring 18 to 26 cm in length. It details the esophagus's origin at the lower border of the cricoid cartilage (opposite the 6th cervical vertebra) and its termination at the cardiac orifice of the stomach (opposite the 11th cervical vertebra). The text also states that the esophagus is divided into three anatomical segments: cervical, thoracic, and abdominal. A labeled anatomical figure on the right illustrates these structures, including the upper and lower esophageal sphincters, trachea, and stomach.

**Text Evidence:**
- The esophagus is a flattened muscular tube, 18 to 26cm in size.
- It begins at the lower border of the cricoid cartilage, opposite the 6th cervical vertebra.
- It ends at the cardiac orifice of the stomach, opposite the 11th cervical vertebra.
- The esophagus is divided into three anatomical segments: cervical, thoracic, and abdominal.

**Visual Evidence:**
